n.story:
Your role remains a bastion of physical skill and situational awareness, largely shielded from the total automation seen in office-based jobs. While the core of your work—the physical act of cleaning glass in unpredictable outdoor environments—remains manual, AI will become a silent partner in your safety and business management. The tedious 'office work' of your job, such as filing activity reports, managing supply inventories, and tracking invoices, will largely vanish into automated, voice-controlled systems.

On the job site, your expertise is amplified by AI-driven risk assessment tools. Before you even clip into a harness, computer vision tools can scan a building's facade to identify structural risks or window damage that the naked eye might miss. You will transition from being a manual laborer to a tech-enabled technician who uses data to ensure maximum safety and efficiency, spending less time on paperwork and more time on high-quality service delivery.

n.story:
Your role is evolving from a purely manual labor position into a technology-enabled facility oversight role. While the core physical tasks of cleaning and sanitizing remain human-centric due to the unpredictable nature of public spaces, the 'invisible' work of the job—tracking supplies, reporting issues, and managing schedules—is being absorbed by AI. You no longer spend time manually counting rolls of paper or filling out paper logs; instead, IoT sensors and smart dispensers feed data directly to your handheld device, telling you exactly where your attention is needed most.

This shift allows you to focus more on the 'attendant' aspect of your title. With administrative burdens removed, you can prioritize high-traffic periods and provide a higher level of customer service and safety oversight. You become a manager of a smart environment, using AI-driven insights to ensure hygiene standards are met more consistently than ever before, while your physical presence provides the human empathy and complex problem-solving that machines cannot replicate.
auto: Manual completion of activity report sheets

Monitoring of supply levels in dispensers
amp: Predictive cleaning based on foot-traffic data
Enhanced health and safety risk assessment
Efficient resource allocation across multiple facilities
n.adv: Focus on becoming proficient with digital facility management tools and smart building interfaces. Your value will increasingly lie in your ability to interpret data alerts and provide a high-quality human presence in a tech-enabled environment.
